test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements with regard to Satnami Movement of Central India.

a) The movement was founded by Ghasidas.

b) The movement was to improve the condition of leather workers.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answers is__** Both a and b**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satnami Movement** was a significant social reform movement that emerged in Central India during the 19th century.
 
• The movement was founded by Ghasidas
 
• This statement is Correct.
 
 
• Ghasidas **was the founder of the Satnami Movement. **
 
• **He was deeply influenced by the teachings of Kabir and aimed at social and spiritual reform. **
 
• **His followers were primarily from lower castes and** oppressed communities.
 
• The movement sought to break the rigid caste system and promote equality, emphasizing devotion to God and self-respect.
 
 
 
• The movement was to improve the condition of leather workers
 
• **This statement is also **Correct.
 
 
• The Satnami Movement f**ocused on improving the condition of not just leather workers but also other marginalized groups such as Dalits, **who faced severe social discrimination.
 
• Leather workers, traditionally seen as an 'unclean' occupation, were among the communities that benefitted from the reformist efforts of the Satnami Movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The movement draws its name from the combination of two Hindi words: "Sat" meaning truth and "Nami" meaning one who carries or spreads.
 
• Satnami followers believe in the unity of God and emphasize the pursuit of truth, equality, and social justice.
 
• The Satnami Movement emerged as a reaction to the oppressive caste system and untouchability prevalent in Hindu society.
 
• Guru Ghasidas, himself belonging to a lower caste, challenged the discriminatory practices and rituals imposed on the lower castes and advocated for their emancipation.
 
• He rejected the notion of caste-based hierarchies and preached the equality of all individuals.
 
• Guru Ghasidas composed various devotional songs and teachings in the form of verses, which are compiled in the religious text called "Guru Granth Sahib."
